promise: The orchestrator hands an agent one entry skill, graphhelm-work. That skill loops: ask GraphHelm next, load next.skill, do the step, record, ask again. A task's status/briefing returns next: {step, skill, actor, because} derived from the task's records. Every step skill ends with its transition table and 'go back to graphhelm-work'. The #2524 wake carries only the task id and 'use graphhelm-work'. A step with no skill or observer returns OBSERVER_MISSING, never success.
proof: PLAN ONLY. Proof at implementation: (a) end-to-end demo task run by agents that received ONLY graphhelm-work: claim -> PR -> review -> BLOCK -> fix -> APPROVE -> merge -> cleanup, each step taken from next, not from memory. (b) journey .graphhelm/journeys/skill-driven-delivery.journey.yaml replays green for each next mapping. (c) conformance test reads every SKILL.md and fails on a transition naming a missing skill or on a mismatch with the Runtime next mapping. (d) break-once: drop one transition row, conformance must fail.

exists: core/execution/src/briefing.rs next_step(): returns NextStep for execution graph nodes only (approve, claim, clear, diagnose, finished), no skill, not delivery steps.
GET /v1/executions/<id>/tasks: already returns stalls[] (block_unanswered, awaiting_verdict, awaiting_merge), owner and liveness.owes. Gives who-owes-what, without skill.
keel.plan record: lists skills, not mapped per step or state.
#2524 (chaser, deadline, wake) and #2531 (cause, unblocker, where): same task-state model; the wake payload should carry next step and skill. This card must not fork that model.
Owner comment on #2582: entry skill graphhelm-work; #2524 wake carries task id only.
plan.cost: Estimate, not measured: next is derived from the task's records for one task, O(records of that task). No scan over all tasks per request.
risks: New public surface: the next field in status/briefing and the tasks endpoint. Needs a named caller (the step skills and Studio).
Compatibility: older clients ignore next; the field is additive.
Idempotency: next is read-only; no write added.
Authority: the author never approves or merges own work; the derivation must not let a claimant see a verdict slot it owns.
Wake payload is only id plus 'use graphhelm-work': the loop depends on next being correct; a wrong next stalls every agent, so the demo task is the gate.
plan.complexity: New mapping function in the Runtime; no existing function made more complex in this plan.

contract.shape: next: {step, skill, actor, because}; step is a fixed enum (claim, implement, review, merge, cleanup, done, diagnose); skill is a name from the transition table or null (null yields OBSERVER_MISSING); actor is an OpenBot actor id or 'owner'; because is a fixed reason code plus the record id it came from.
contract.where: new task-level function next_task_step(TaskState) in core/execution/src/tasks.rs, called from status/briefing and as a per-task field in GET /v1/executions/<id>/tasks. briefing.rs next_step stays for execution nodes; the two stay separate.
reads: blocked: blocked_by (+ cause, unblocker, where from #2531)
contract.one_model: blocked is the owner heartbeat with cause, unblocker, where; next.step for a blocked task is review or implement by the named unblocker; the #2524 wake carries the same next block. Names agreed with #2531; reason stays the stall enum.
